analysis.investment_thesis: MIDHANI fails both legs of the Magic Formula: earnings yield of ~3% (vs. 12%+ threshold) signals extreme overvaluation, while ROIC of ~12.6% is well below the 20%+ minimum for a "good business." With net profits actually declining at -2.7% CAGR over six years, the market is paying a premium for a deteriorating earnings profile.
key_strengths: Strategic defense/aerospace PSU with captive demand — sole domestic producer of superalloys and titanium alloys for ISRO, DRDO, HAL
Gross margin of 60.3% reflects genuine pricing power in specialized, import-substitution materials with no commodity exposure
Capex cycle winding down (CWIP collapsed from INR 549 Cr to 24 Cr); FCF turned decisively positive at INR 149 Cr in FY25
key_risks: Earnings yield ~3% (EBIT INR 219 Cr / EV ~INR 7,237 Cr) — the Magic Formula would rank this in the bottom decile on cheapness
ROIC ~12.6% (EBIT / invested capital of ~INR 1,740 Cr) — PSU inefficiencies keep returns well below the 20% threshold needed to justify a premium
Finance costs have compounded at 27.4% CAGR (INR 7 Cr → 30 Cr), pressuring a net profit that has fallen from INR 177 Cr (FY22) to INR 111 Cr (FY25) despite revenue growing 25% over the same period
red_flags: P/E of 63x on declining earnings (-2.7% net profit CAGR) — classic overvalued PSU re-rating with no earnings support
EV/EBITDA of 33.45x for a business with 13.7% operating margins and EBITDA that hasn't grown in 3 years (INR 250 Cr FY25 vs. INR 292 Cr FY22)
Operating cash flow was negative in FY23 (-INR 35 Cr); positive FY25 figure of INR 217 Cr partly reflects working capital release, not structural improvement
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Magic Formula verdict is unambiguous: MIDHANI fails on both required dimensions. Earnings yield of ~3% is four times below my 12% threshold — you are paying INR 7,237 Cr of enterprise value for INR 219 Cr of EBIT. Even on a forward basis (using the implied Forward P/E of 38.5x), earnings yield barely reaches ~4.5%, still a failing grade. ROIC of ~12.6% using invested capital of ~INR 1,740 Cr (equity + debt - cash) is below my 20% floor for "good business" designation. A high-quality special materials franchise should generate 25%+ on tangible capital; MIDHANI does not, largely because it carries a bloated asset base (INR 2,950 Cr assets for INR 1,074 Cr revenue, implying asset turns of 0.36x).

The underlying business narrative is sympathetic — a strategic PSU with real moats in defense-grade superalloys and titanium — but narrative does not equal returns. Net profit has compounded at -2.7% annually since 2019 while revenue crept up at 7.1%, which means the company is getting worse at converting sales into profit. Finance costs have nearly quadrupled over six years, consuming margin gains. The government promoter holding of 74% and strategic importance may provide a valuation floor, but at 63x trailing earnings the stock requires a sustained earnings re-acceleration that the last several years of data simply do not support. The Magic Formula would rank this near the bottom of any large-cap screen.
